string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of the People\'s Republic of China and one of the country\'s four direct-administered municipalities. It is a major political, cultural, and educational centre, home to national government institutions, universities, museums, and historic sites such as the Forbidden City and the Great Wall. Beijing has a long history as an imperial capital and today combines traditional neighbourhoods with modern business districts and transport networks. It hosted the 2008 and 2022 Olympic Games and is an important hub for international diplomacy, research, and technology.

Shanghai is a direct-administered municipality and China\'s largest city by urban population. Located on the Huangpu River near the Yangtze estuary, it is a leading financial, trade, shipping, and manufacturing centre. The city is known for the Bund, Pudong\'s skyline, historic lilong neighbourhoods, and a vibrant cultural scene. Shanghai has long been an international port and remains one of Asia\'s most globalised cities. It hosts major universities, research institutions, and international events, and its economy spans finance, technology, logistics, and advanced services.

Chongqing is a direct-administered municipality in southwest China, located where the Yangtze and Jialing rivers meet. It is one of China\'s largest municipalities by area and population, with a landscape of hills, rivers, and mountains. Chongqing is an important industrial, transport, and logistics centre and a major node for the Yangtze River Economic Belt. The city is known for spicy hotpot, historic wartime sites, and dramatic urban scenery. It has developed rapidly through manufacturing, technology, trade, and infrastructure projects, while also preserving distinctive regional culture.

Tianjin is a direct-administered municipality in northern China and a major port city on the Bohai Sea. It lies close to Beijing and serves as an important gateway for trade, shipping, and industry in the region. Tianjin has a history of foreign concessions, visible in its varied architecture, and is known for the Hai River, ancient cultural street, and modern economic zones. It is a centre for advanced manufacturing, logistics, finance, and education. The city also plays a key role in the coordinated development of the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region.
